name: Week 16 Push — Steady State (Spotlight: Lateral Raise + Kinesis Fly)
description: Volume steady, loads steady. Spotlights cycle forward to the DB lateral raise + Kinesis cable fly — the two shoulder-isolation lifts due for a deep-cue refresh, and the two that feel best on the right shoulder right now. Push press runs early when the rack's free (it recovers reps there); tempo is your energy lever — fast-drive or slow-eccentric, your call by feel. Chest press keeps the cross-body arm stretch between sets. Cable lifts list a number per equipment option.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state — sets and loads hold. Spotlight cycles forward to DB lateral raise + Kinesis fly. Push press runs early when the rack's open; tempo (fast-drive vs slow-eccentric) is your energy lever. Chest press keeps the cross-body stretch between sets. Pull-up greasing + protective shrug stay in the warmup.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. The last set's final reps have been breaking form at 15lb. Spotlight drills lead-with-the-elbow + the 2s eccentric so all three sets hold clean at 15, and bakes in the scap-reset-between-sets habit that quiets the shoulder.

Cycles forward — last spotlighted W12. This is the lift the right shoulder/pec likes best — the slow-eccentric stretch reads as relief, not pain. Spotlight drills the fixed soft elbow + the deep loaded stretch, the most shoulder-friendly pec work on the day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W13 cable column block · W14 push press + incline DB · W15 chest press + farmer carry · W16 lateral raise + Kinesis fly (current) · W17 cycle forward — push press + incline DB refresh.
watchpoints: **Run push press early when the rack's free** — it recovered to 8/10/8 there. If it ends up second after a long warmup trail, expect ~7/6/6 at 45 — that's the accepted trade-off for getting the session in.
**Tempo is your energy lever** — fast-drive (bank energy for later) or slow-eccentric (more stimulus). Pick by feel; neither is the 'right' one. Form holds either way.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — two straight pain-free weeks. Don't chase load while the streak is alive. (Distinct from the DB lateral raise spotlight — the day has both.)
**Pack DOWN, not up** — push press, both lateral raises, incline DB, chest press, farmer carry all carry the cue. If a lockout needs a shrug, the load's too heavy for the cue — pause the set.
**Chest press: cross-body arm stretch between every set** — proactively, it keeps the right pec quiet. The win on chest press is a quiet pec, not the rep count.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective behind-back shrug stay in the warmup** — both cheap, both easy to forget. Part of the weekly pull-up + shoulder-decompression frequency.
**Cable block lists a number per machine** — pick what's free, log the equipment + number you used.

sets.name: Warmup + Shoulder Rehab (Non-Negotiable) + Pull-Up Greasing + Protective Shrug

exercises.notes: Slow, big circles. Wake up scap glide before loading.
Full sequence with red band. Non-negotiable on push day.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension — dials a stretch up the back chain from forearm to shoulder. Wakes the grip and shoulder line before loading.
Ribs down, glutes tight, body in one line. Slow eccentric, 1s pause with chest 1-2" off the floor.

**Pull-up greasing set.** 1 fresh set, slow tempo, NOT to failure. Active hang start, pull elbows down to ribs, chest leads. Frequency, not max effort — drop to scapular-pulls only if the shoulder talks, and finish the count.

**Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set, DBs held behind the body, palms back. Pack the shoulders DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s peak squeeze, slow down. The 'opposite movement' that decompresses the right shoulder — costs no time, easy to forget.

**LOAD:** 45lb DBs per side. 3 sets of 8-10 (7/6/6 is fine if these run second — see the order watchpoint).
- **Feet parallel, hip-width** — not duck stance
- **Ribs DOWN before the dip** — catch any rib flare on set 1
- **Pack DOWN, not up** — shoulder blades into the back pockets, neck long
- **Shallow dip ~3-4"**, straight down through the heels
- **Vertical DB path** — DBs travel up next to the ears, head pokes through at the top
- **Tempo is your call** — fast-drive to bank energy, or slow eccentric for more stimulus. Drive fast, lockout solid; the descent matches the tempo you pick. Breath: in at the dip, out on the drive

**LOAD:** 15lb DBs. 3 sets of 15-18.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — make all three sets hold the form, not just the first two:**
- **Lead with the elbow, hand passive** — the wrist follows the elbow, the hand never lifts first
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED** through the whole rep — a locking/unlocking elbow recruits the traps
- **'Pour the water out of two cups'** at the top — a hair of internal rotation, pinky leads up
- **Stop at shoulder height — never higher.** Higher just shrugs the traps off the medial delt
- **2s eccentric** — the slow descent is the entire stimulus; fight the drop
- **Scap reset between sets** — roll the shoulders, actively engage/disengage the scapula a few times before the next set. This is what's kept the right shoulder quiet here.

**Reflection:** the last set's final reps have been breaking down at 15. Does the scap reset + a strict 2s eccentric hold the form clean to the end of set 3, or does it still break? If it breaks, that's the honest ceiling at 15 — hold, don't add load.

sets.name: Incline DB Press (3 Sets at 45 pair)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45lb pair. 3 sets — run the controlled-descent version that landed best (10-12 with a pause at the bottom + a controlled, not-quite-slow descent).
- **Bench at 30°**, not 45° — steeper biases front delt over upper chest
- **Shoulders packed back AND down** — pin the back of the shoulder into the bench
- **Forearm stacked vertically over the elbow at the bottom** — the cue that makes 45 feel honest
- **Elbows ~45° from torso**, not flared to 90°
- **1s pause at the bottom** ('dead weight'), press to a fingerwidth apart at the top. Breath: in on descent, out on press

**LOAD:** 165. 3 sets.
- **Seat height: handles at the mid-chest / nipple line** — set it before sitting; the wrong height loads the front of the shoulder
- **Shoulders pinned BACK against the pad** — hold it the whole set
- **Tempo is the lever:** on a genuine 3s slow eccentric, 6 clean reps is the honest number here — don't force the rep count to match a fast-tempo week. The win is the right pec staying quiet, not the reps.
- **Press to almost extension** — leave a hair of bend
- **Ribs down** — no arching off the pad
- **🔁 BETWEEN EVERY SET: cross-body arm stretch on the right side** — pull the arm across the chest, 20-30s. Do it proactively; it's kept the right pec quiet.

If 165 craters below ~5 on a slow eccentric and the pec stays quiet, that's fine — you're strong-enough here and the management goal is met. Drop to 150-155 only if you want the higher rep count back at the slow tempo.

**LOAD:** Kinesis 9 (the working number now — drop to 8 only if 9 feels off on set 1).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the shoulder-friendly pec stretch, drilled:**
- **Slight forward hinge at the hips** — chest leads, not the head
- **Soft elbow ~10-15°, FIXED throughout** — these are NOT presses; the elbow angle never changes
- **'Hug a tree'** — the squeeze comes from the chest, not the arms pulling together
- **Stop a fistwidth apart at the top** — don't crash the handles; the last inches are arm work
- **Slow eccentric (~3s)** — let the cables pull the arms back into the deep pec stretch. The right shoulder/pec likes this stretch — it reads as relief, that loaded-lengthen 'everything stretching out' feeling. Protect that.

**Reflection:** does the slow loaded stretch keep the pec/shoulder feeling relieved (not pinched) across all 3 sets at 9? If it does, this is the template for shoulder-friendly chest work — note what the stretch feels like.

sets.name: Cable Column Block — Lat Raise → Tri Ext → Straight-Arm Pulldown (3 Rounds)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 30** (hold — two pain-free weeks running)
- **Kinesis: 5-6** (the W9-swap default, if the column's taken)

3 rounds, one arm at a time.
- **Lead with the elbow as a DIRECTION** — the elbow points, doesn't bend
- **Soft elbow ~10°, FIXED** throughout
- **Stand sideways** to the stack, working arm farther from it
- **Stop at shoulder height — higher = traps**
- **2s eccentric**, fight the cable down

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 70** (default)
- **Kinesis: 5** (fallback)

3 rounds. **Always kneeling — there's no bench at this station; the forward torso lean IS the 'incline.'**
- **Kneel facing AWAY from the high pulley**, rope overhead
- **Elbows PINNED** — only the forearms move
- **Hands shoulder-width on the rope**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the rope pull the hands behind the head
- **Stop just shy of lockout**, slow eccentric. Set 1 feels easy, set 3 is brutal — that's the lift working.

**LOAD:**
- **Cable column: 120** (the working number — really hard here)
- **Kinesis: 6** (fallback)

3 rounds.
- **Stand a step back, hinge ~15° at the hips** — fixed hinge, the torso doesn't pump
- **Slight elbow bend (~5°), FIXED throughout**
- **Pull the bar to the thighs, NOT past** — past = shoulders roll forward, lats switch off
- **Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom** — 'oranges into the back pockets'
- **Slow controlled return to a full overhead stretch.** Hold 120 — reps may fall on the later sets; that's the load biting, not a problem.

sets.notes: Cable block — sharp cues, 3 rounds. One trip to the chosen station covers all three. Pick what's free (cable column is the default for all three) and log what you used.

sets.name: Farmer Carry (3 Walks)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50lb DBs. 3 walks of ~45-60s each — chase hold-time now that 50 is the load and the shoulder stays neutral.
- **Stand TALL** — ribs down, crown reaching up, no leaning back
- **Shoulders pulled DOWN and BACK** — into the back pockets, never shrugged toward the ears. The DBs pull the shoulders up the whole walk; resist the whole walk
- **Neck long, eyes forward** — no chin poke
- **Grip firm but NOT death-clenched** — grip is the limiter here (it taps out before the shoulder), so let it be the trainable edge; set the bells down when grip fails rather than white-knuckling
- **Walk a straight line at a deliberate pace**, breathing steadily

sets.notes: Trap-chain + grip block. 3 walks at 50lb — packed-shoulder posture, and grip as the honest edge. Set them down when grip gives, not before.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every-Gym-Day Closing Block)

exercises.notes: 30s each arm at MID elbow position. Pec minor lengthen — the antagonist to the upper-trap chain loaded all session.
Passive hang from the pull-up bar. **Don't engage** — let the shoulders unpack and the spine decompress.
30s each side on the mat. Draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Front leg + back leg at 90°. Sink the hips toward the floor — hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift before leaving the gym.

sets.notes: 5 minutes of recovery work, non-negotiable closing block.

tips: **Steady state — sets and loads hold.** The work is depth of execution at the established numbers.
**Spotlight: DB lateral raise + Kinesis fly.** Lateral raise drills the elbow-lead + 2s eccentric so all 3 sets hold at 15; Kinesis fly drills the shoulder-friendly loaded stretch at 9.
**Run push press early when the rack's free.** Tempo (fast-drive vs slow-eccentric) is your energy lever — pick by feel.
**Cable lateral raise holds at cable column 30** — two pain-free weeks; don't chase load.
**Cross-body arm stretch between every chest-press set** — proactively. A quiet pec is the win, not the rep count; 6 clean slow-eccentric reps at 165 is honest.
**Pack DOWN, not up** — every press + the carry carries the cue.
**Pull-up greasing set + protective shrug in the warmup** — 1 slow set each, not to failure.
**Farmer carry: 50lb, chase hold-time** — grip is the edge; set them down when grip gives.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, permanent every gym day.**
Rest: 2 min push press + chest press, 90s lateral raise + Kinesis fly + farmer carry, 75s cable block.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state push week — the gains come from sharper execution at established loads, not chasing weight. The lateral raise and Kinesis fly get the deep-cue treatment because they're the two shoulder-isolation lifts that feel best on the right side right now: drilling the elbow-lead and the loaded stretch is shoulder-management work as much as it's hypertrophy. Building decades, not weeks.
